124	## Unresolved
125	
126	**Does Safari on iOS carry an https certificate bypass to `wss://` on the
127	same origin?** No vendor statement. Against: Apple Developer Forums, iOS
128	26 beta 3, certificate accepted, WebSocket failed with "The certificate
129	for this server is invalid" (https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/792842;
130	reporter says beta 5 resolved it); WebKit bug 158345 (NEW, last 2021):
131	"you need to do a normal page load first", WebSockets ran on CFStream
132	outside the Network process (https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=158345);
133	two blogs: "accepted the cert for HTTPS, but not WSS"
134	(https://www.hotelexistence.ca/ios-safaris-websockets-implementation-doesnt-work-with-self-signed-certs/,
135	https://gist.github.com/apankrat/612dde3d7f01c4713c9579b0a94d9547, which
136	works only with a trusted CA and SANs). Queries: `iOS Safari self-signed
137	certificate "visit this website" WebSocket wss fails after accepting
138	certificate warning`; `bugs.webkit.org WebSocket wss self-signed
139	certificate iOS Safari fails "certificate for this server is invalid"`.
140	Line: the page must work without the socket, polling `/api/v1/waiting`
141	and the collections by revision over `fetch` when the socket fails or
142	closes; the socket is an upgrade when it connects. If the owner's phone
143	connects, the poll becomes a slow fallback.
144	
145	**Does an iOS Safari bypass persist across tabs and relaunches?** No
146	source states a duration; the gist calls acceptance "temporary". Query:
147	`iOS Safari self-signed certificate warning exception persist across
148	tabs relaunch "This Connection Is Not Private"`. Line: the page must
149	lose nothing when the warning returns, and the dialog says it may
150	return. If it persists, nothing changes.
151	
152	**Are `Secure` cookies stored and sent on a bypassed-certificate
153	origin?** "Secure" is user-agent defined; no vendor statement found.
154	Query: `Chrome cookies Secure attribute set over https page with
155	certificate error bypassed interstitial`. Line: the end-to-end test uses
156	the host's own client and proves the host side only; the page must show
157	"pair again" when its first authenticated call after `/pair` is 401, so
158	a dropped cookie is a visible state. If cookies work, nothing is added.
159	
160	**Does a browser retry a page-load `GET` whose connection the host
161	dropped under the four-connection cap?** Chromium reviews show retries
162	only for a closed reused socket (https://codereview.chromium.org/403393003,
163	https://codereview.chromium.org/174287); nothing current for Safari.
164	Query: `Chrome retry GET request connection closed before response
165	reused socket ERR_CONNECTION_CLOSED`. Line: the unauthenticated page
166	load needs fewer parallel connections than `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (4)
167	less one for `/info` and `/pair`: one HTML plus at most one CSS and one
168	JS, and the plan states the count. If browsers retry, the count holds.
169	
170	**Does `history.replaceState` keep the code out of history and sync?**
171	MDN-derived text says it does not prevent a global history entry; no
172	vendor statement. Query: `history.replaceState does Chrome browser
173	history record original URL before script runs`. Line: the code is
174	single-use and the window closes on first success
175	(`docs/remote-client.md:310`), so a code in history after pairing is
176	spent; the plan says so, and closes the window on the page's failure
177	report or the five minutes. A fragment keeps it out of server logs, not
178	history.
179	
180	## For the owner
181	
182	**Does the iPhone Camera open `https://<ip>:<port>/?code=…` in Safari
183	with the query intact, and Chrome on Android?** No Apple document covers
184	IP-literal URLs (query: `iPhone Camera app scan QR code opens Safari URL
185	with query string`). If yes, the URL is the only invite; if not, the
186	text beside the QR is the URL to paste. Both work with the URL as the
187	single payload.
188	
189	**After accepting the warning on the owner's phone, does
190	`new WebSocket("wss://<ip>:<port>/api/v1/events")` connect?** Decides
191	whether the poll is the fallback or the path; both work with the poll
192	built.
193	
194	**Does the bypass survive closing the tab and relaunching Safari?** Both
195	branches work with the warning sentence in the dialog.
196	
197	**Is a 49-module QR at 4 px per module readable at arm's length?**
198	Today's is 57 modules at the same scale, so no harder; if not,
199	`QR_SCALE` rises.
200	
201	**Does the owner's Mac have a VPN or Tailscale taking the default
202	route?** If so the QR's address is the tunnel's and unreachable from the
203	phone; the plan may list every non-loopback interface and let the owner
204	pick. If not, the one address is right.

# Correctness review, round 1 (head abe87c6)

The Rust side matches the plan. I found no contract or SCHEMA_VERSION problem, since no serialized type changed. Cookie auth, the clearing 401, the `transport: cookie` pairing, the page routes and the rate window all do what the plan says. Three defects are in `web/app.js`. I read the code only; I did not run the page or the Swift tests.

## 1. A rotated key locks the page out of re-pairing (`web/app.js:109-112`)
`start()` checks `stored.server_id === info.server_id && stored.spki_sha256 !== info.spki_sha256`. If that matches, it shows "identity changed. Pair again." and returns, before it looks at the invite.
- State: the browser paired earlier, and the host then rotated its key. The server id is kept across a rotation (`make_identity` is called with `Some(server_id)`), so `stored` still matches by id and differs by key.
- Input: the owner opens the new QR or invite URL. `takeInvite()` has already cleared the fragment. The page shows the "Pair again" notice and posts nothing.
- Result: `localStorage` is only rewritten after a successful pair, so every later scan hits the same branch. The page tells the user to pair again and makes pairing impossible until they clear site data.
- Plan step 2 says to send nothing else when the key differs *without* a fresh invite. The code applies it to a fresh invite too.
- Fix: when an invite is present, compare `invite.key` with `info.spki_sha256` and pair. Show "identity changed" only when there is no invite.

## 2. A refresh requested during a refresh is dropped, and it can stay stale (`web/app.js:157-160`, `:332-334`, `:351`)
`refresh()` returns at once if `state.refreshing` is set. An event whose revision is above `state.rev.projects` calls `refresh()` and gets no retry.
- State: the socket is live, the poll timer skips because `state.live`, and a refresh is in flight.
- Input: a session starts waiting after the in-flight `GET projects` or `.../sessions` was answered, and its `changed` frame arrives before the refresh ends. That second `refresh()` is a no-op.
- Result: the list keeps the old waiting flag. Nothing retries until the next event, and the poll is suppressed while `live`. The "waiting first" view, the point of the feature, can be wrong for an unbounded time on a quiet host.
- Fix: set a `dirty` flag when `refresh()` is called while one is running, and run once more when it finishes.

## 3. A revoked or never-paired device is not shown as such if `/projects` or the poll answers 401 later (`web/app.js:162-165`)
`refresh()` shows "revoked" on a 401, and returns without stopping the interval or closing the socket.
- Result: `schedule()` keeps calling `refresh()` every 5 s once the socket is down. The next call replaces the notice.
- Result: a later non-200, non-401 reply, such as a 503 from a full pool, returns early without touching the notice.
- Effect: the notice survives only until the next `render()`, which a socket `onclose` or `onopen` triggers (`render()` at `:195` rebuilds `main`). A revoked device's notice is therefore replaced by the stale session list on the next socket event, because `render()` redraws `state.sessions`.
- Fix: on 401, set a `state.dead` flag, stop the timer and close the socket, and have `render()` return early on it.

## Not a defect
- The event revision comparison at `:332` is sound. The host has one global revision, so the `projects` reply's revision is comparable with an event's.
- Bearer-first auth, the clearing 401 and the unreachable no-cookie case in `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3153-3178`) match the plan.
- `limited()` counts any method on `/`, `/app.css` and `/app.js` against the page window. A `POST /` is a 429 rather than a 404 after 120 hits. It is harmless.
